professional_summary.short_bio: Audio designer for games. I build interactive music systems in Wwise/FMOD, design sound for animation, and write tools that solve real production problems. Specializing in horror game audio, ML-based audio classification, and real-time DSP.
professional_summary.extended_bio: Game audio designer working with Wwise/FMOD and C++/Python. I build audio systems within performance and memory limits. Voice management, memory budgets, optimization. Adaptive music, horror sound design, pipeline tools.
professional_summary.philosophy: Sound should serve the experience, not demand attention. Every audio element, from subtle ambience to explosive SFX, exists to enhance gameplay clarity, emotional impact, and player immersion. Technical precision meets creative intuition.

clarity_first.title: Clarity First
clarity_first.description: Audio in games needs to be clear. I check telemetry—what does the player need to hear right now? Mix hierarchy, frequency separation, ducking. Player gets info, not noise.

technical_limits.title: Know Your Limits
technical_limits.description: Understanding limits helps: voice counts, memory, CPU. I build systems that work in prototype and scale to production without breaking budget.

layering_parameters.title: Layers & Parameters
layering_parameters.description: I design sounds in layers: transient for punch, body for weight, texture for character. Then hook parameters (speed, intensity, distance) to blend them in real-time. Sounds react to gameplay.

collaboration.title: Iterate with Feedback
collaboration.description: Audio needs input from designers, programmers, and players. I document systems, explain decisions, and iterate based on playtests. Audio ships when the game ships.

featured_projects.title: Not Today, Darling!
featured_projects.tagline: Race Against Time. Outsmart Your Grannies. Win Big!
featured_projects.short_description: Retro-inspired audio implementation for chaotic multiplayer racing game.
featured_projects.detailed_description: 3-layer adaptive music in Wwise. Layers change with player count and race intensity. Kept music coherent under tight voice limits.
featured_projects.role: Audio Designer — Full audio pipeline (sound design, Wwise integration, implementation)

audio_systems.metasounds: Procedural audio system - layers change with speed and game state, pitch/filters controlled by parameters
audio_systems.sfx_system: Track materials blend smoothly (asphalt/sand/metal), hazard sounds pitch down based on camera and speed
audio_systems.mix_strategy: Priority system: UI/gameplay (1.0) > player SFX (0.8) > crowd (0.5)
audio_systems.integration: Sound Cues with parameters, Submix buses, Concurrency limits, Master limiter

challenges_solved.problem: With 4 players, sounds stacked up and UI became inaudible
challenges_solved.solution: Limited max collision sounds to 4. Each player gets different EQ range. Crowd ducks when UI plays

challenges_solved.problem: Moving between surfaces (asphalt sand metal) caused audio pops
Boost sounds used too much memory (160MB with 4 players)
challenges_solved.solution: Switched to procedural MetaSounds. Now uses <2MB per player

featured_projects.title: Amorak
featured_projects.tagline: Horror animation about a man who outsmarts a beast. Creature roar layered from lion, elephant, tiger, and hippo sounds.
featured_projects.short_description: Atmospheric soundscapes and creature audio for horror animation.
featured_projects.detailed_description: Creature sound design. 15+ vocal variations, procedural footsteps, environmental audio that reacts to creature proximity. Built in Reaper.
featured_projects.role: Sound Designer — Creature vocals, foley, ambience design and mix

audio_approach.creature_roar: Layered roars from lions, elephants, tigers, and hippos, then processed and pitched down. Low rumbles (40-120Hz) for physical presence, mid-range snarls for aggression
audio_approach.basement_atmosphere: Dripping water, creaking wood, rattling chains, scurrying rats. Thunder rumbles outside. Each element placed spatially
audio_approach.narrative_support: Sound follows emotional arc: quiet carving thunder tension violent door smash heavy footsteps silence trapdoor slam payoff rolling apple victory

technical_details.frequency_work: Creatures at 40-200Hz for body, environment fills mid-range, highs for tension
technical_details.spatial_mix: 3-layer ambience system (distant/mid/close) with auto crossfades based on camera distance, 300ms smoothing
technical_details.dialogue_clarity: Dynamic ducking -8dB when dialogue plays, carved 1-3kHz notch in ambience, boosted dialogue at 2.5kHz

challenges_solved.problem: Beast needs low-end presence but it fought with environmental rumble
challenges_solved.solution: Environment sits at 60-90Hz, creature at 120-180Hz. Notch filter at 80Hz when creature on-screen. Dynamic EQ boosts creature +3dB during roars

challenges_solved.problem: Camera jumps between wide and close-ups made ambience sound jarring
challenges_solved.solution: Built 3-layer ambience system with auto crossfades, 300ms smoothing on level changes

featured_projects.title: Transientica: AudioLab
featured_projects.tagline: ML-powered beatbox recognition for rhythm gaming
featured_projects.short_description: Real-time ML beatbox classification with 45ms latency.
featured_projects.detailed_description: Real-time ML beatbox classification. 45ms latency. Python/TensorFlow pipeline, 2000+ sample dataset.

technical_achievements.pipeline: Spectral-flux for onset detection, SVM for classification
technical_achievements.optimization: Smaller FFT window (512 samples, 11ms), circular buffer eliminates I/O blocking, lightweight SVM (2ms vs 15ms neural net)
technical_achievements.architecture: Separated audio and ML threads, lock-free ringbuffer, audio on high priority thread

challenges_solved.problem: First version had 180ms lag - too slow for rhythm games
challenges_solved.solution: Optimized pipeline: smaller FFT window, circular buffer, lightweight SVM, UDP for OSC. Got to 45ms with 92% accuracy

challenges_solved.problem: Both have transients and noise - lots of wrong guesses
challenges_solved.solution: Added spectral centroid, zero-crossing rate, envelope shape features. Separate models for solo vs patterns. 78% to 92% accuracy

challenges_solved.problem: Heavy ML caused buffer underruns on weak CPUs
challenges_solved.solution: Separated threads with lock-free ringbuffer. Audio never blocks, ML on worker thread

featured_projects.title: Pause & Deserve
featured_projects.tagline: A psychological horror experience where every pause comes with a price
featured_projects.short_description: Psychological horror game with strategic pause mechanics.
featured_projects.detailed_description: Horror audio that watches how you pause. Audio state machine in Unity. Tension builds during pauses, music gets more unsettling when you hesitate.

audio_systems.reactive_audio: Time manipulation effects - pitch shifts downward, reverb extends when pausing. Audio escalates with Death's proximity and speed
audio_systems.spatial_audio: 3D audio positioning tracks Death's location through sound alone
audio_systems.psychological_tension: Sub-bass frequencies (ultra-low 20-60Hz) you feel more than hear, strategic silence amplifies sudden sounds, false footsteps for misdirection

soundscape_design.oppressive_atmosphere: Low-frequency drones, distant cries, unsettling textures
soundscape_design.proximity_system: Audio intensity rises as Death approaches, heartbeat pounds when danger is near
soundscape_design.environmental_shifts: Walls shift, echoes change, spaces transform - all with unique sounds

game_mechanics.chase: Death relentlessly pursues, learns patterns, adapts strategy
game_mechanics.pause_mechanic: Freeze Death temporarily but it becomes faster afterward
game_mechanics.shifting_world: Environment never static - walls close in, paths rearrange
